readingInstruction: Read John 18:1-19:16. Jesus is arrested in a garden, questioned, denied by Peter, tried before Pilate, and sentenced to be crucified. Notice who is really in control, and the conversation about kingship and truth.
settingTheScene: After the prayer, Jesus crosses the Kidron valley to a garden, where Judas arrives with soldiers and officials. John tells the story of the trial from a different angle than the other Gospels. He leaves out Gethsemane’s agony and the Jewish council’s formal verdict, and emphasizes Jesus’ sovereignty. The key scenes are the confrontation in the garden, the interview with Pilate, and the cry of the crowd.
observation: “Put your sword into its sheath; shall I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?” (18:11).
“Peter again denied it, and at once a rooster crowed” (18:27).
“My kingdom is not of this world” (18:36).
“Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice” (18:37).
“You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above” (19:11).
interpretation:
When the soldiers come, Jesus steps forward: “Whom do you seek?” “Jesus of Nazareth.” “I am he.” And they draw back and fall to the ground. Even in his arrest, his majesty shows. He asks them to let his disciples go, and they do. Peter strikes with a sword, and Jesus says, “Shall I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?” He is not a victim of events. He is going to the cross willingly.

Peter follows at a distance. In the courtyard, he is asked whether he is a disciple, and he denies it. Three times. Then a rooster crows. Meanwhile, inside, Jesus is questioned by Annas and then Caiaphas, and struck by an officer.

Before Pilate, the leaders do not enter the Gentile governor’s headquarters so they will not be defiled before Passover, a terrible irony as they seek the death of the innocent. Pilate asks, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answers, “My kingdom is not of this world.” It is a real kingdom, but it does not rely on swords. “For this purpose I was born… to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.” Pilate’s famous answer is a question, “What is truth?” He is standing in front of the Truth and does not know it. He tells the crowd three times that he finds no guilt in Jesus.

Pilate has Jesus flogged, and the soldiers put a crown of thorns on his head and a purple robe on him. Pilate brings him out: “Behold the man!” The King wears a crown of thorns, and he is exactly the man we need. When the leaders cry “Crucify him!”, Pilate says, “You take him and crucify him.” They say he has made himself the Son of God. Pilate becomes more afraid. “Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?” Jesus answers, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above.” God is in control, and yet Pilate and the leaders are guilty.

Finally the chief priests say, “We have no king but Caesar.” The people who had longed for centuries for God to be their King now renounce him. Pilate hands Jesus over to be crucified. The innocent Lamb is handed over on the day of preparation for the Passover, at the very hour the Passover lambs were being slaughtered.
connection: Exodus 3:14 is the “I am he” that made the soldiers fall back. Isaiah 53:7-8 describes the silent servant. Psalm 2:1-6 describes the nations raging against the LORD’s anointed. Daniel 7:14 gives the Son of Man a kingdom. Exodus 12 is the Passover lamb. 1 Timothy 6:13 says Christ Jesus made the good confession before Pilate. Romans 5:8 says Christ died for us while we were sinners. Acts 2:23 says he was delivered up according to the definite plan of God.
application:
Reflect on Peter’s denial and Jesus’ willingness to restore him. Bring any denial of your own to Jesus.

Ask what it would mean to let Christ be your King in an area you’ve kept for yourself.

Meditate on “Behold the man!” for a few minutes in silence.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for going willingly to the cross.
Confess where you have not listened to his kingdom’s call.
Ask him to teach you to belong to his kingdom.
